title: GM–eVAC split highlights demand-side risk in US magnet buildout
gist: GM cancelled its long-term NdFeB magnet supply deal with eVAC Magnetics (Vacuumschmelze's US unit) after a 29% drop in its H1 2026 US EV sales, triggering arbitration. The article (truncated by paywall) frames this as demand-side risk for the US magnet buildout.

insights.claim: General Motors has cancelled its long-term rare earth permanent magnet supply agreement with eVAC Magnetics, the US unit of Germany's Vacuumschmelze, prompting an arbitration dispute.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Offtake contracts underpinning US magnet plants can be unwound when OEM volumes fall; counterparty demand risk matters for ex-China magnet equities.

insights.claim: A termination notice was issued on 1 July 2026 and eVAC began arbitration days later, alleging wrongful termination and seeking financial compensation.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Watch the arbitration outcome as a precedent for enforceability of take-or-pay style magnet offtakes.

insights.claim: The contract, signed in early 2023, covered a minimum ten-year supply of NdFeB permanent magnets from the Sumter, South Carolina plant, which has 2,000tpa capacity.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Loss of the anchor customer puts utilisation and economics of a 2,000tpa US magnet plant in question.

insights.claim: GM's US EV sales fell 29% in H1 2026 versus H1 2025, which preceded the magnet contract cancellation.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Weak US EV demand is transmitting upstream to critical-mineral and magnet supply chains built around OEM offtakes.
insights.quote: a 29% fall in US EV sales for GM in H1 2026 compared with H1 2025

insights.claim: The article's title frames the split as evidence of demand-side risk in the US magnet buildout, not only supply-side risk from China.
insights.speaker: Benchmark Team
insights.so_what: Policy-supported ex-China capacity still needs end-demand; favor magnet projects with diversified customers beyond EVs.
